messages:
zara: Heads-up: we're proposing a header rename to reduce collisions and shorten client wiring. Current: `X-Redwood-Route`. Candidate: `X-RW-RouteIntent`. Thinking dual-emit for a few releases, then flip. Thoughts?

nate: Shorter name SGTM. Dual-emit avoids breaking middleboxes that look for the old header. We should define clear ordering in backends: prefer new header for attribution when present.

julia: Console and billing pipelines need to be tolerant. If both headers present we must ensure attribution is deterministic. Also: add a flag in the SDKs to opt-in to emit the new header only for canary builds so we can measure before broad rollout.

riley: From an ops POV, please add an aggressive adoption metric and a per-customer fallback. Some customers still use proxies that strip unknown headers. We should log header-presence per-request (sampled) so we can map customer infra that might require support.

zara: Plan proposal: 1) SDKs (py/ts/go) add RW_NEW_ROUTE_HEADER env var; when set to 1 emit both headers, when set to 2 emit only new header (canary); default stays old header for initial minor release. 2) Edge proxy shim maps new->old for 45 days. 3) Console ingest accepts both, sets a new metadata field `route_header_seen` with values `old`, `new`, `both`. 4) After adoption threshold (85% across production traffic and no unknown-route spike), flip default in SDKs and deprecate old header after 60 days.

nate: Implementation notes: in Python client we have to watch for header normalization: requests/urllib3 lowercases header keys in some places. Suggested snippet for py: 

```python
# http_client.py
route_val = route_hint
headers = {"x-redwood-route": route_val}
if os.getenv("RW_NEW_ROUTE_HEADER") == "1":
    # dual emit
    headers["x-rw-routeintent"] = route_val
elif os.getenv("RW_NEW_ROUTE_HEADER") == "2":
    # canary-only: only new header
    headers = {"x-rw-routeintent": route_val}
resp = session.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
```

julia: For TypeScript/Node: note that some frameworks normalize header keys to lowercase automatically. Make sure our middleware doesn't collapse two logical headers into one entry. Also add unit tests that assert both header names are set when RW_NEW_ROUTE_HEADER=1.

riley: Ops: We'll deploy an edge-shim that does mapping plus logs metric `route.header.adopted` (sampled 0.1%) with fields `sdk`, `sdk_version`, `customer_id`, `header_seen`. That should let product/console show adoption by SDK. We'll also add an alert if `header_seen` is `none` for >2% of traffic (i.e., headers missing).

zara: Good. For quota attribution: prefer the new header when both present. That prevents double-counting or split attribution. Need to update the quota service and run a small backfill to label historical hits as `old`.

nate: Backwards-compatibility: the dual-emit approach is safest. But check caches and CDNs that dedupe headers; if a CDN collapses same-name headers, the new name avoids that but some intermediaries may drop unknown names. That's why the shim is important.

julia: Docs/SDK changelog: include migration snippet, env var semantics (0 = old-only default, 1 = dual-emit, 2 = canary-only), and a removal timeline. Also mention header length limits and recommend keeping route hints short (<512 bytes).

riley: Ops request: add a slow-path recorder when header length > 1024 bytes to avoid blowing up telemetry pipelines. Tag those requests as `route.header.long` with sampling 1.

zara: Timeline: SDK minor release with dual-emit toggle -> target in 7 days. Edge-shim to staging today (ops will roll). Console ingest + adoption tile -> parallel roll in 10 days. Evaluation at 6 weeks to decide flip.

ops-bot: edge-proxy/shim v3 scheduled to deploy to staging 2026-03-24T16:00:00Z

nate: I'll draft PRs for py/ts/go with the env var and tests; will add the canary docs.

julia: I'll update the console ingestion manifest and add the small adoption tile on the rollout dashboard.

riley: I'll add ops runbook notes for customers with header-stripping proxies and how to enable shim mapping per-tenant.

zara: Thanks everyone. I'll write the migration doc and send a short email to customers who use custom proxies. Closing this thread; reopen if needed.
